note: Ground truth for benchmark/supabase-notes/app (Next.js on Supabase, with Firestore whiteboards). Never copy this file into the audited directory. Same format and matching rules as benchmark/answer-key.json: `locations` are files relative to app/ with 1-based inclusive line ranges of the vulnerable statement or of the code a fix changes; a finding matches by its primary location only (window, nearest entry wins). When a real finding is scored as unmatched, check the range against the code, then fix the key, not the finding.

seeded.class: Table exposed through the Data API without Row Level Security
seeded.why: public.note_shares never gets `enable row level security`, so anyone holding the public anon key can read every share (who shares which note with which email) and insert shares to give themselves access.

seeded.class: RLS select policy `using (true)` on private data
seeded.why: "notes: readable" lets every signed-in user read every note; the note page selects by id only and relies on that policy.

seeded.class: RLS update policy checks login, not ownership
seeded.why: "notebooks: members rename" uses auth.role() = 'authenticated' with no WITH CHECK, so any user can rename any notebook or set owner_id to themselves.

seeded.class: SECURITY DEFINER RPC without ownership check or search_path, executable with the anon key
seeded.why: share_note() bypasses RLS, never compares the note's owner with auth.uid(), keeps the default EXECUTE grant to PUBLIC/anon and has no fixed search_path: a caller shares any note with themselves.

seeded.class: Storage policies scoped to the bucket, not to the owner
seeded.why: Any signed-in user can list, download and add objects anywhere in the private attachments bucket; nothing ties the object path to the note owner.

seeded.class: Service-role key shipped to the browser (NEXT_PUBLIC_ and imported by a client component)
seeded.why: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is inlined into the client bundle via share-dialog.tsx; the service role bypasses every RLS policy.

seeded.class: Edge Function without JWT verification trusts a user id from the body
seeded.why: export-notes runs with verify_jwt = false and a service-role client, and exports the notes of whatever userId the caller sends.

seeded.class: Firestore rules: signed-in is treated as owner
seeded.why: Any signed-in user can read, change and delete every board and its strokes; only create checks ownerId.

seeded.class: Storage rules `allow read, write: if true`
seeded.why: exports/ is world readable and writable: anyone can read, overwrite or host arbitrary files under exports/ in the project bucket.

seeded.class: Callable Cloud Function without an auth or ownership check (App Check is not authorization)
seeded.why: deleteBoard uses the Admin SDK (bypasses rules) and deletes any board and its files by id; enforceAppCheck only proves the call came from the app, not who made it.

decoys.why: plans is a public price catalogue with no personal data; `using (true)` for select is intended.
handle_new_user is a SECURITY DEFINER trigger function with `set search_path = ''`; trigger functions cannot be called through the Data API.
The owner-update policy is scoped to auth.uid() and column grants limit updates to display_name and avatar_path, so email cannot be changed.
The browser updates a note by id only, but the update policy restricts USING and WITH CHECK to owner_id = auth.uid().
SECURITY DEFINER with `set search_path = ''`, filters by auth.uid(), EXECUTE revoked from public and anon.
avatars is public by design; uploads and replacements are limited to the caller's own folder.
The service-role client is server-only (`import "server-only"`, non-public env name) and deletes only the authenticated user's own account.
The Supabase anon key and the Firebase web config (apiKey included) are public by design; access is decided by RLS and rules.
verify_jwt = false is right for a provider webhook; the function verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature over timestamp and raw body with a 5-minute window before any write.
Thumbnails check the board's ownerId through firestore.get(), plus size and content type on writes.
renameBoard checks request.auth and the board's ownerId before writing.
